turns.doctor_question: Hi, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Nice to meet you too. Well, I'm here because I keep having these moments where things just feel... unreal. 

I'll be sitting in my own house, or at my desk at the office, and it's almost like I'm watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there in my own body. It's very unsettling, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.

symptom_reasoning.S082: The patient describes feelings of unreality and an out-of-body sensation of watching themselves from across the room, which directly characterizes depersonalization and derealization.

turns.doctor_question: When these unreal moments happen, do you still know that it’s just a feeling and that you’re actually in your body and surroundings?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. I mean, logically I know I'm still sitting right there at my desk. I know I haven't actually left my body or anything. It's just a really strange sensation while it's happening, but... yeah, I do know it's just a feeling.

turns.doctor_question: When these unreal feelings come on, do they happen during sudden surges of intense fear or panic?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I don't feel panicked or terrified when it happens. It's more of a... detached feeling, I guess. Just strange and uncomfortable, but not a sudden rush of fear.

turns.doctor_question: Before these unreal or detached moments started, had you gone through a traumatic event?
turns.patient_response: Yes. Actually, this has all been going on for about two weeks now... ever since a client threatened me in my office.

turns.doctor_question: Since the client threatened you, have you been having unwanted memories of it that keep coming back?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't really had that. I mean, I think about it sometimes, sure, but it's not like the memories are just popping into my head when I don't want them to. It's not playing on a loop or anything like that.

symptom_reasoning.S069: The patient explicitly denies experiencing involuntary, intrusive memories of the threatening event popping into their head.

turns.doctor_question: Since the client threatened you, have you been having nightmares about it?
turns.patient_response: No, no nightmares. I've actually been sleeping okay, for the most part. Just... no bad dreams about it that I can remember.

symptom_reasoning.S027: The patient denies having nightmares and reports sleeping well for the most part, ruling out sleep disturbance.

turns.doctor_question: Since that threat happened, have you been feeling constantly on guard or watchful?
turns.patient_response: Yes, definitely. Even when I'm just at home in Roanoke, I find myself tracking every little noise. I'll hear a car door shut outside, or a footstep on the porch, and I'm instantly focused on it. And if I'm out somewhere, I'm always checking where the exits are. It just feels like I constantly need to be ready, you know, in case someone tries to come at me again.

symptom_reasoning.S079: The patient explicitly confirms feeling constantly on guard, tracking every noise and checking for exits to be prepared in case someone attacks again, demonstrating hypervigilance.

turns.doctor_question: Since the client threatened you, have you been avoiding reminders of what happened?
turns.patient_response: No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I still go into the office every day and meet with people. I haven't been staying away from work or... avoiding certain places, if that's what you mean. I pretty much just go about my normal routine. I'm just a lot more careful while I'm doing it.

symptom_reasoning.S070: The patient explicitly denies avoiding places, people, or routines associated with the traumatic event.

turns.doctor_question: Since the client threatened you, have you ever felt as if the event were happening again in the moment?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't had anything like that. I mean, I definitely think about what he said, but I don't ever feel like I'm actually back in that moment or that it's happening all over again right then. It just stays a memory.

turns.doctor_question: Since the client threatened you, do reminders of what happened make you feel intensely upset?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean, if I come across a tax file that reminds me of him, or someone happens to mention his name, I don't get intensely upset. I don't enjoy thinking about it, obviously, but it doesn't make me panic or break down or anything like that. It's more just that general feeling of being on edge that I mentioned earlier, rather than getting really upset over specific reminders.

turns.doctor_question: Since the threat happened, have you been unable to remember an important part of what happened?
turns.patient_response: Actually, yes, there is a gap. I remember him crowding me in my office, and I clearly remember the police being there afterward. But the middle part... like, what he actually said right before I reached for the phone... is just a blank. No matter how hard I try to pull it up, I just can't remember that specific part.

symptom_reasoning.S071: The patient explicitly confirms having a memory gap for an important part of the traumatic event, describing that what happened right before reaching for the phone is a complete blank.

turns.doctor_question: Are these unreal or detached episodes causing problems in your daily life or work?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, they really are. Um, I've actually missed several client deadlines recently because of it. And I've pretty much stopped seeing people at the office altogether. I just... I don't trust myself to handle their tax returns properly right now, and I definitely don't feel like I can keep the workplace safe. So, yes, it's having a big impact on my work.

turns.doctor_question: Since the threat happened, have you been feeling unable to experience positive emotions, like feeling happy or loving toward other people?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I have noticed that. It's... it's strange. Like, my wife tries to joke with me, or she asks about going fishing like we had planned to do, and I know those are things that should make me feel good. But right now, it's just like the part of me that enjoys them has been switched off. I just feel flat.

symptom_reasoning.S076: The patient explicitly confirms feeling that the part of him that experiences positive emotions and enjoyment has been switched off, describing feeling flat.

turns.doctor_question: Did all of this start within the past month?
turns.patient_response: Yes, it did. It's, um... it's been going on for about two weeks now, right ever since that client threatened me in my office.

turns.doctor_question: Besides that blank spot in your memory, are you unable to remember an important part of the threat itself?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, that's exactly it. I remember him crowding me in my office, and I remember the police being there afterwards. But that middle part... what he actually said right before I reached for the phone... it's just a blank. No matter how hard I try to pull it up, I just can't remember that specific part.

symptom_reasoning.S071: The patient explicitly confirms having a blank spot and being unable to remember an important part of the traumatic encounter despite trying.

turns.doctor_question: When something reminds you of the client who threatened you, does your body suddenly react strongly?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I obviously don't like thinking about him or what happened, but my body doesn't do anything... extreme. I don't get a racing heart or start sweating or anything, if that's what you mean. It's just more of that flat feeling I mentioned.

turns.doctor_question: Since the threat happened, have you had unwanted memories of it suddenly come into your mind?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean, I think about it sometimes, sure, but it's not like the memories are forcing their way in or anything. It's just... I know it happened, but I'm not having sudden flashes of it popping into my head out of nowhere.

symptom_reasoning.S069: The patient explicitly denies experiencing intrusive memories or sudden flashes of the event popping into their head.

turns.doctor_question: When that client threatened you, did you believe at the time that he might seriously injure or kill you?
turns.patient_response: No, I didn't think he was going to kill me or anything like that. I mean, he was definitely angry, and he was way too close to me, which was intimidating. But I didn't think my life was in danger or that he was going to severely hurt me. It was just a really aggressive and threatening situation.
